module_title: Biology in Human Welfare: Common Diseases & Microbes in Everyday Life
introduction: This foundational level explores the biological agents that cause sickness in humans and contrasts them with the beneficial microbes utilized in households and industries. Memorizing the causative agents, vectors, and diagnostic tests for common diseases is the absolute first step for NEET.

core_concepts.title: Common Bacterial and Viral Diseases
core_concepts.description:
1. Typhoid: Caused by the bacterium Salmonella typhi. Spreads via contaminated food/water. Symptoms: Sustained high fever ($39^\circ\text{C}-40^\circ\text{C}$), weakness, stomach pain, intestinal perforation in severe cases. Diagnostic test: **Widal Test**.
2. Pneumonia: Caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae. Infects the alveoli (get filled with fluid). Spreads by inhaling droplets/aerosols. Symptoms: Fever, chills, cough, severe cases show bluish lips/fingernails.
3. Common Cold: Caused by Rhino viruses. Infects the nose and respiratory passage but STRICTLY NOT the lungs. Lasts 3-7 days.

core_concepts.title: Protozoan, Fungal, and Helminthic Diseases
core_concepts.description:
1. Malaria: Caused by Plasmodium (P. vivax, P. malaria, P. falciparum - most fatal). Vector: Female Anopheles mosquito.
2. Amoebiasis (Amoebic dysentery): Caused by Entamoeba histolytica (protozoan in large intestine). Vector: Houseflies. Symptoms: Stools with excess mucus and blood clots.
3. Ascariasis: Caused by Ascaris lumbricoides (intestinal roundworm). Symptoms: Internal bleeding, muscular pain, blockage of the intestinal passage.
4. Elephantiasis (Filariasis): Caused by Wuchereria (W. bancrofti and W. malayi). Vector: Female Culex mosquito. Causes chronic inflammation of lymphatic vessels of lower limbs.
5. Ringworm: Caused by fungi Microsporum, Trichophyton, and Epidermophyton. Symptoms: Dry, scaly lesions with intense itching.

core_concepts.title: Microbes in Household Products
core_concepts.description:
1. Curd: Lactic Acid Bacteria (LAB) like Lactobacillus convert milk to curd. LAB produces acids that coagulate and partially digest milk proteins. It improves nutritional quality by increasing **Vitamin B12** and checks disease-causing microbes in the stomach.
2. Dough & Bread: Fermented by Baker's yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae). The puffed-up appearance is due to $CO_2$ gas production.
3. Toddy: A traditional drink of Southern India made by fermenting sap from palm trees.
4. Cheese: Swiss cheese has large holes due to massive $CO_2$ production by Propionibacterium sharmanii. Roquefort cheese is ripened by a specific fungus.

core_concepts.title: Microbes in Industrial Products
core_concepts.description:
1. Fermented Beverages: Saccharomyces cerevisiae (Brewer's yeast) ferments malted cereals and fruit juices to produce ethanol. Wine and beer are produced WITHOUT distillation (low alcohol). Whisky, brandy, and rum are produced BY distillation of fermented broth.
2. Antibiotics: Chemical substances produced by some microbes that kill/retard the growth of other disease-causing microbes. Penicillin (from Penicillium notatum) was the first antibiotic discovered by Alexander Fleming (used heavily in WWII to treat American soldiers).

important_entities.name: Bioactive Molecules
important_entities.key_fact: Microbial products with specific medical/industrial applications.
important_entities.significance:
1. Streptokinase: Produced by Streptococcus (modified by genetic engineering). Used as a 'clot buster' for patients who have undergone myocardial infarction.
2. Cyclosporin A: Produced by the fungus Trichoderma polysporum. Used as an immunosuppressive agent in organ-transplant patients.
3. Statins: Produced by the yeast Monascus purpureus. Used as blood-cholesterol lowering agents (they competitively inhibit the enzyme responsible for synthesizing cholesterol).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Alexander Fleming discovered Penicillin by observing a mold (Penicillium notatum) inhibiting the growth of Staphylococci bacteria. However, he did NOT establish its full potential as an effective antibiotic. Its full potential was established later by Howard Florey and Ernst Chain. All three shared the Nobel Prize in 1945.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Remember 'MET' to identify the specific fungal genera responsible for Ringworm. Do not confuse them with macroscopic fungi like mushrooms or plant pathogens.

exam_strategy_tips: Always distinguish between the vectors. Female Anopheles = Malaria. Female Culex = Filariasis (Elephantiasis). Female Aedes = Dengue and Chikungunya. Housefly = Amoebiasis.
